title: Afghan Woman Deported in Historic First Use of US Alien Terrorist Removal Court
detail: An Afghan woman was deported in what US officials describe as the first-ever use of the Alien Terrorist Removal Court (ATRC), a secretive federal tribunal created in 1996 under the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act that had never previously been exercised to remove anyone. The ATRC allows the government to deport individuals using classified evidence that neither the subject nor their defense counsel can fully review, bypassing normal immigration court proceedings. The case marks a significant and historic legal precedent in US immigration enforcement and national security law.

media.caption: Afghan woman deported in the first-ever use of the US Alien Terrorist Removal Court, marking a historic legal precedent.

title: Six Charged After Anti-ICE Protest Outside Atlantic City Police Headquarters
detail: A protest outside Atlantic City, New Jersey police headquarters on Saturday, September 12, 2026 grew out of a September 9 dispute in which an Atlantic City police officer pulled over a vehicle driven by Cristian Moreno-Rodriguez, founder of the community group El Pueblo Unido, as he followed vehicles the group believed were ICE transporting a detained community member toward a Newark-area detention facility. Roughly 100 demonstrators gathered September 12 chanting against 'the kidnappings of our community' and alleged local police cooperation with ICE; the protest escalated when demonstrators blocked access to the Public Safety Building. Police charged or issued complaints against six people: Moreno-Rodriguez (obstruction of justice), Keli Smith (obstruction of justice and resisting arrest), Diana Chaparro (simple assault), Jose Salazar (simple assault and illegal possession of a chemical device), Anthony Diaz (obstruction of justice), and Devon Barber (simple assault). Atlantic City Police Chief James Sarkos denied his department assisted ICE and released surveillance footage of the September 9 stop, saying the officer had observed dangerous driving.
